synopsis: VaViM was a Swedish six-month pre-study running from February to August 2022, involving Volvo Autonomous Solutions and Blekinge Institute of Technology and funded through Vinnova and Drive Sweden [f15705, f1552]. It studied virtual-model validation for autonomous vehicles in fenced areas, produced a feasibility model, and is identified as the nearest precedent for transferring on-road simulation methods to off-road machines [f15706, f1250, f15715]. The booklet describes comparative physical tests as both produced and planned, while describing side-by-side use of validated models and real tests as a conclusion, a long-term goal, and an implemented method; those differences leave the extent of implementation unclear [f1551, f1722, f1251, f1723, f1931]. Its transferable lesson is to adopt automotive-style credibility concepts without assuming automotive sensor and environment models are valid off-road [f1724, f15716]. Six months did not establish an accepted virtual-validation capability: the VaViM/EVIDENT comparison reports funder acceptance but no approval, and marks validation time after capability establishment as not applicable; the broader reference class supports planning capability development in years [f1552, f1932, f1930, f15713, f15717].
